audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers print Fiora winning six of seven rows. The packet reads Skill / Fiora / Fiora / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Fiora, and the prose agrees with the packet everywhere the two differ: whys[0] 'play it even' (Skill, printed Fiora), whys[3] 'Coin-flip window' (Skill, printed Fiora), whys[4] 'Six is his swing' (Cho'Gath, printed Skill), whys[5] 'his health bar outgrows your burst window' (Cho'Gath, printed Fiora).
audit.why: A six-row Fiora sweep on a 50.83% lane over 360 games is not what any of the underlying text describes. The page was telling the player they win a coin-flip and win the row its own explanation calls his swing.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill 5 / Fiora 7 / Fiora 7 / Skill 5 / Cho'Gath 4 / Cho'Gath 4 / Cho'Gath 4 in both layers, with all seven phases[].why rewritten to state their new side. diffRating raised from 4/10 to 5/10 and report[2], report[7], report[14] and breakdown.difficulty brought in line.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why said 'Ravenous Hydra is your spike — force fights the moment it completes' on the first-item row, which both the packet and whys[5] give to Cho'Gath, and no cooldown appeared anywhere in the full layer.
audit.why: Feast is 80/70/60s — the shortest-cooldown ultimate in the matchup against your 110s Grand Challenge, which is why the level-6 row swings to him. Rupture is a flat 6s at every rank and 950 range, so it returns faster than your 13s rank-1 Lunge. Feral Scream is 11s at rank 1 in a 300-range cone.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, phases[5].why, phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5].t and the full layer generally say only 'Telegraphed. Dodge or Riposte it' about Rupture, and the dontsFull bodies are the same generic filler under three different titles.
audit.why: Rupture is the one interaction in this matchup that is a certainty rather than a maybe: it is a knockup, and Riot's Riposte text stuns if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect — so parrying Rupture returns a stun, not a slow. That is worth stating plainly, and it is the single best reason to hold a 24s cooldown. Feast is permanent max Health on a kill, so denying his stacks is a wave-management instruction, not a vague warning.
audit.corrected: report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns now state the knockup-to-stun certainty; dontsFull[0..2].d rewritten to their own titles with Rupture's range and cooldown, Feral Scream's cone range, and the permanence of Feast stacks.
sources: enemyKit R text (grows, gaining maximum Health)

audit.why: Two things the local data cannot settle, so I made no claim about either: whether Feral Scream's silence counts as an immobilizing effect for the Riposte stun upgrade, and whether Riposte's parry actually blocks Feast's true damage. The content layer already asserts the second ('Feast is ONE damage instance, so your Riposte CAN block the cast') in spikes[1].text, mid and wants.you[2]. I did not repeat it in anything I wrote and did not delete it. The mirror audit flagged the same two gaps.

notes: The full layer had Fiora winning six of seven rows on a 50.83% lane whose own prose says level 6 is his swing and the two-item 1v1 goes to him. Chart corrected in both layers. Row 6 is the one place I departed from the packet, which lists Fiora at two items — see questionsForUser; three separate content strings (whys[6], spikes[3].text, late) all say Cho'Gath wins the long 1v1, so I followed the prose rather than invent a power shift the page then contradicts three times. I left the content layer's claim that Riposte can block Feast's cast in place but did not repeat it: Riot's Riposte text says it parries all incoming damage, and Feast is a single instance, but nothing in the local data confirms the true-damage execute is parryable specifically, and it is the kind of claim a player will bet a life on.
